title: img.naturalWidth is density-corrected for x-descriptor srcset — breaks any 'naturalWidth/cssWidth' DPR/resolution QA formula
body: Found while re-verifying CORE-6965 (T6): the task's prescribed re-measurement formula ("effective DPR = naturalWidth / rendered CSS width", at deviceScaleFactor 2) produced a false negative on images that were ALREADY correctly fixed. ## Root cause Per the HTML/WHATWG spec, `HTMLImageElement.naturalWidth`/`naturalHeight` for an image selected via an `x` density descriptor in `srcset` (e.g. `foo.png 1x, foo-2x.png 2x`) report the **density-corrected** intrinsic size — i.e. the real decoded pixel width DIVIDED by the selected density — not the raw byte dimensions of the file that was actually downloaded and rendered. This matters directly for this codebase: `src/components/Media/ImageMedia/index.tsx` sets `sizes = sizeFromProps ?? (widthFromProps ? undefined : '100vw')` — i.e. any `` / `next/image` usage that passes a fixed `width`/`height` and no explicit `sizes` (the common pattern for fixed-size logos/icons, e.g. `src/blocks/BankingPartners/BankingPartnersView.tsx`) gets Next's `x`-descriptor srcset form (`?w=64 1x, ?w=128 2x`), not the `w`-descriptor/`sizes` form. Concretely, for the CORE-6965 bank-partner logos (58px CSS box, 116px 2x master): after the CMS fix landed, `img.naturalWidth` read exactly `58` (== cssWidth == cssWidth), which by the naive formula computes `effectiveDPR = 58/58 = 1.0` — i.e. LOOKS exactly like the pre-fix, broken state, even though the browser genuinely fetched and decoded the full 116×116 byte master. This was reproduced and confirmed via independent fetch+decode: `fetch(img.currentSrc)` → `await blob()` → `await createImageBitmap(blob)` gave `bitmap.width === 116` for the exact same resource the `` element reported `naturalWidth: 58` for, on multiple assets, consistently. ## Why it matters beyond T6 Any future QA/measurement task (this one plus, notably, **CORE-7133**, the no-`vw` `sizes` byte-waste ticket already flagged as adjacent) that measures "is this image served at N× resolution" via `naturalWidth / cssWidth` on a fixed-width `next/image` (x-descriptor srcset, the common case sitewide per `ImageMedia`'s `sizes` fallback logic above) will get a **false negative** — it will report a correctly-2x-served image as still 1×, and a worker/agent could chase a phantom regression or, worse, "fix" something that isn't broken. ## What to do When a future task's AC prescribes measuring served-image resolution via `naturalWidth`, replace the formula with a byte-accurate measurement: ```js const currentSrc = img.currentSrc || img.src const resp = await fetch(currentSrc) const blob = await resp.blob() const bitmap = await createImageBitmap(blob) const effectiveDPR = bitmap.width / img.getBoundingClientRect().width ``` This reads the TRUE decoded pixel width of the exact response the browser is displaying, unaffected by density-descriptor correction. Worth adding as a documented helper/snippet (maybe in `clone-qa-tools`) so it isn't re-derived from scratch each time a resolution-QA task comes up — this took real diagnostic time on T6 (fetch+decode cross-check, network-response logging, multiple repro scripts) before the spec behavior was identified as the cause rather than a real regression. ## Evidence See T6's report (reports/T6-1.md, field 4 and field 10) for the full diagnostic trail: repeated measurements on the Vercel preview for `fix/core-6965-image-resolution`, `_next/image` request logging showing only ONE network request per asset (ruling out a stale-cache explanation), and the fetch+decode cross-check proving the served bytes were correct while `naturalWidth` reported half that value. prod/clone URLs used: https://rapid-formations-clone-git-fix-core-6965-image-315b4b-bsq-group.vercel.app/ (home page, BankingPartners + CustomerQuote/testimonial sections).
